Now to India, where opposition parties marched to the Supreme Court in the capital on Monday,
calling for the resignation of the country's election commissioner.
Opposition leaders accused the election chief of purging India's voter list to favor Prime
Minister Narendra Modi, NPR's Amkar Kantakar reports.
Demonstrations against India's election chief have led to a sweeping crackdown across the
country, with the police detaining hundreds and locking down parts of the capital over
the weekend.
But on Monday, thousands converged in New Delhi from across the country to demand their voting
rights.
The march ended as opposition leader Rahul Gandhi filed a petition in the Supreme Court
to stop and audit an ongoing exercise that deleted more than 130 million names of India's
voter lists.
The ruling BJP party rejects allegations against Modi and election commissioner Kyanesh Kumar.
Neither of them commented on the protests.
Omkar Kantakar, NPR News, New Delhi.
This is NPR News.
